title: Recording Hello Dolly in December 1963
summary: Joe says Hello Dolly was his biggest hit; it was cut for Kapp on December 4, 1963, and Glaser expected You've Got a Lot of Living To Do to be the hit.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: That's nice. Tell me about 'Hello, Dolly.'
Heh-heh, that in itself was a funny story.
Before we start that, would you say 'Hello, Dolly' was the biggest hit record that you've ever been on? I'm not talking about under your name. I'm just talking about the most...

Oh, no question about it. No question about it. Because this thing was so big, you couldn't believe it. And it stayed big for a long time. The thing about it, Joe Glaser was friends with Jack Kapp of Kapp Records, and I think...
Well, no. Kapp. That was the label. Kapp Records.
Oh. I thought Jack Kapp was working for Decca.
He probably maybe had something to do with Decca. But the first release of...

It was on the Kapp label. It was made December the 4th, 1963. And then Louis didn't particularly care for it. I think the reason why Joe Glaser did it had something to do with that show. I think Joe might have had a piece of that show, or for whatever reason. But the tune
